expected_symptom: Access-violation/assert internal_failure compiling hs_6_6 with two unreferenced module-scope globals (arithmetic float3x3 const, static Texture2D<float4> array); DXIL-only per the one maintainer comment.
history: regressed-in v1.6.2106 (last good: v1.6.2104, oldest release expressing hs_6_6); reproduces in every stable release through v1.9.2607 (newest catalogued) and on main-debug
reviewed_by: gpt-5.3-codex (independent batch-019 step-10 review; applied selectively at collation)
summary: Still reproduces on main-debug (89e2f98e29c289ae8ad9e00dd310104fea9fd7df): compiling the filed hs_6_6 hull shader traps assert(Index < Length) in llvm::ArrayRef<Value*>::operator[], called from StoreVectorOrStructArray during HLSL SROA (SROA_Helper::RewriteForStore), rewriting a store into the unused Texture2D array global before it is eliminated as dead -- confirms and pins down Keenuts 2023-01-26 comment. Continuing past the trap (gh) hits an access violation in the same chain, so Debug-assert and Release-AV are one defect. DXIL-only: identical -spirv compile is clean. bisect: v1.6.2104 clean (oldest release expressing hs_6_6), regressed-in v1.6.2106 (exact stderr/address match to the reporter v1.7.2212 quote), reproduces through v1.9.2607 (newest stable) and CE dxc_trunk (cast<X> E_FAIL form). Re-testing the reporter ARRAY_SIZE table as hypotheses: only size 0 is clean today; size 2, which the report called ok, now crashes like every other non-empty size -- a broader form of the same bug, not a weaker one.
title: Compiling hull shader with unused globals causes internal compiler error
